rows.Notes: The confirmed claim is: 'Product-Market Fit gets you customers. Promise-Market Fit gets you believers.' Short form: LinkedIn headline and meta description (decided May 26). Mid form: About paragraph and /vcs/ hero (not yet written). Long form: foundational essay or position page (not yet written).
rows.Task: Draft short, mid, and long form versions of the category claim

rows.Notes: Read 10-15 platform-lead posts from target firms. Catalog the words they use for the function we serve. Name from what's already in their vocabulary before introducing new language.
rows.Task: Listen-before-naming pass: collect language the target tier already uses

rows.Notes: Pick three named partners. Write what they read in 30 seconds on the current front door. Reverse-engineer language that would pass it. This is the foundational test the rest of the build runs on.
rows.Task: Draft the 30-second test against three named target firms

rows.Notes: Walk the homepage, about, work, and any landing surfaces with a tier-1 partner in mind. Mark exactly where the read drops to creative agency. Capture verbatim language that needs replacement.
rows.Task: Audit current sightbox.co against the 30-second test

rows.Notes: The comparison set is consultative counsel, not creative production. Does the claim read at that register without overclaiming the McKinsey label? Where does it slip back into agency vocabulary?
rows.Task: Stress-test the claim against the McKinsey/Deloitte register

rows.Notes: LinkedIn is the most discoverable surface for the target tier. Treat the headlines and About copy as front door.
rows.Task: Audit current LinkedIn copy (Sightbox and Nathan) against the 30-second test

rows.Notes: Does AI survive as the external front door at the new altitude, or is it a frame inside a larger claim? The May 2026 work brought it closer to the right register. Decide whether it carries or needs reframing.
rows.Task: Test Authored Intelligence as front-door category

rows.Notes: Once the claim has settled, the working drafts and decisions compile back into the canon as the new front-door reference. Substrate gets richer.
rows.Task: Compile category claim decisions back into canon

rows.Notes: Working hypothesis: no. PNP is internal scaffolding. The external claim is its own artifact. Confirm or revise.
rows.Task: Decide: does PNP language ever appear in external surfaces

rows.Notes: Downstream of the single-sentence claim. The hero is the literal 30-second test. Should be the last thing rewritten, not the first.
rows.Task: Rewrite sightbox.co homepage hero

rows.Notes: The one sentence that makes a Forerunner or Sequoia partner say oh I should read more instead of oh creative agency. Conviction-grade. Must pass the can't un-hear test.
rows.Task: Write the single-sentence claim

rows.Notes: Whatever decks are currently in active circulation. Mark which ones route to the wrong slot at the first slide.
rows.Task: Audit the standing decks against the 30-second test

rows.Notes: Bi-weekly is the target. Monthly is the floor. Decide what's actually sustainable alongside the rest of the practice. The rhythm is the asset, not any individual piece.
rows.Task: Set the publishing cadence for Field Notes

rows.Notes: Who gets each piece, in what sequence, with what framing line. Distribution discipline. The asset is the LinkedIn network of thousands of VCs plus reachable X surfaces. Use it deliberately, not broadcast-style.
rows.Task: Build the distribution playbook for each Field Notes piece

rows.Notes: Pieces 2 and 3 of the rhythm. Each one calibrated against the Judgment Layer piece. Don't ship if it doesn't pass the forward test.
rows.Task: Publish Field Notes piece 2 and piece 3

rows.Notes: Not vanity metrics. The signals that matter: who shared, who commented at altitude, which named partners or platform leads engaged, whether any inbound traces back. Compile after each piece.
rows.Task: Track performance signals on each published piece

rows.Notes: PMF is now the external front door. Authored Intelligence, if pursued as a position paper, is a secondary asset — the foundational essay that sits behind the claim, not the claim itself. Lower priority than the first Field Notes piece.
rows.Task: Draft the Authored Intelligence position paper

rows.Notes: Decided May 26, 2026. Promise-Market Fit is the confirmed external front door. Authored Intelligence is secondary — candidate for a standalone position paper or foundational essay, not the front door. The task below captures that work if pursued.
rows.Task: Decide where Authored Intelligence fits in the publishing structure

rows.Notes: Sightbox-owned site, LinkedIn, X, guest placements. Decide the canonical home and the syndication pattern. Where each piece lives, in what order, with what hook.
rows.Task: Decide the venue strategy

rows.Notes: Working backwards from the brief: the next two quarters should produce 8-12 Field Notes pieces. Pull from Nathan's existing thinking. Quick inventory pass before structuring a queue.
rows.Task: Inventory 8-12 ideas already alive in Nathan's thinking

rows.Notes: Two quarters in, walk the published pieces and assess. What landed at altitude. What didn't. What the queue should look like for the second half of the year.
rows.Task: Mid-build review of the publishing rhythm

rows.Notes: Set up a place to capture observations from client work, reading, conversations that could become pieces. Atlas-style capture. Walk the queue weekly for coherence.
rows.Task: Stand up the topic queue with capture rhythm

rows.Notes: 3-5 named partners at target firms. The dual-readership test: would a platform lead forward this to a GP and would the GP be glad to receive it. Write to specific people, not an audience.
rows.Task: Name the imagined readers for each Field Notes piece

rows.Notes: Order matters. Which piece does the most credentialing work first? Which piece reaches the imagined readers most directly? Sequence is half the strategy.
rows.Task: Name the next 3 Field Notes pieces and sequence them

rows.Notes: Within 30 days of starting the build. Calibrate to the Judgment Layer piece: would a Sequoia platform lead forward this to a partner? If not, it's not ready.
rows.Task: Publish the first Field Notes piece of the 4.0 rhythm

rows.Notes: Where do the three case studies live? Replace the existing portfolio framing or sit alongside it? Decide the home, the order, the framing copy that surrounds them.
rows.Task: Decide where the 3 case studies live on sightbox.co

rows.Notes: Strategic clarity is hard to measure. Second-order effects on hiring, fundraising, retention, product decisions are more tractable. Audit what each candidate can substantiate before committing to the narrative.
rows.Task: Audit measurable outcomes for each candidate engagement

rows.Notes: Case study language that surfaces from the writing often sharpens the category claim. Walk back through and compile what surfaced. Substrate compounds.
rows.Task: Compile case study language back into canon

rows.Notes: Walk the 50+ companies on sightbox.co/startups. Mark 5-7 candidates for case study depth. Not the biggest logos. Not the most recent. The ones that best demonstrate Sightbox at altitude.
rows.Task: Identify 5-7 candidate engagements from the existing portfolio

rows.Notes: From the 5-7, narrow to 3. The three that prove the practice at the new altitude. The selection conversation is part of the work. RethinkCare is a stated candidate.
rows.Task: Narrow to 3 case studies for first-pass write-up

rows.Notes: Case studies 2 and 3 follow the framework prototyped on RethinkCare. Each one tested against the partner-reader bar: what would they actually ask, and does the piece answer it.
rows.Task: Draft case study 2 and case study 3

rows.Notes: Once the three are out, the case study layer has to handshake with the category claim (claim being proved) and the Field Notes (thinking that produced the work). Walk the connections. Make them legible.
rows.Task: Cross-link case studies to category claim and Field Notes

rows.Notes: Prototype the framework here. Relationship and context are freshest. If RethinkCare works, the other two follow the pattern.
rows.Task: Draft the RethinkCare case study

rows.Notes: Explicit list of which engagements are NOT featured. The portfolio is large; the curated set is small and deliberate. The discipline of not featuring is part of the strategic posture.
rows.Task: Document which engagements are deliberately NOT featured

rows.Notes: The four-question structure already drafted on the page: strategic problem, what Sightbox saw that others didn't, what changed measured in outcomes, what's durable. Plus narrative shape. Build the template once, then apply to each case.
rows.Task: Build the case study framework

rows.Notes: An on-record client voice multiplies credibility significantly. Identify who from the client side could be quoted at depth for each of the 3. Approach individually with care.
rows.Task: Identify client-side voices willing to be quoted on-record

rows.Notes: Within first 2-3 weeks of the build, not deferred. Frame forward: here's the tier we're building for. Not backward: here's what's been wrong. Charlie's commercial instincts are an asset at the right altitude. Schedule when both principals are rested.
rows.Task: Hold the Charlie conversation about the front door

rows.Notes: Once warm-intro architecture is built, sequence the first 3-5 warm intro attempts. Not all at once. One at a time, with care, with the right Field Notes piece in hand as the artifact behind the intro.
rows.Task: Sequence the first warm intro attempts

rows.Notes: Tier A (first 6-month window, 12 firms): Forerunner Ventures, Lerer Hippeau, Costanoa Ventures, Spark Capital, True Ventures, Homebrew, Cowboy Ventures, Greycroft, Defy Partners, BoxGroup, M13, Founder Collective. Left off: USV (upper edge), NEA/Greylock/Bessemer/Bond (above the line/in-house), Founders Fund/Lightspeed/Khosla (too partner-dependent), IVP (later-stage), Floodgate/Pear/Susa/Maveron (too small or limited platform posture), Battery (likely in-house), Initialized (quiet platform posture), Foundry Group (wound down new investments).
rows.Task: Name Tier A: the 8-12 firms in the active 6-month window

rows.Notes: Existing relationships ride out as they are. No new acquisition energy at the current tier. As inbound arrives from the current tier, apply the decline script and route gracefully. Note each instance for pattern recognition.
rows.Task: Log current-tier inbound and how each was handled

rows.Notes: What does it sound like when a current-tier VC approaches us for design work. Gracious but clear. Frames forward toward referral, doesn't burn the relationship. Charlie should be involved in shaping this.
rows.Task: Draft the decline script for wrong-tier inbound

rows.Notes: Six months in, re-evaluate Tier A. Which firms moved up. Which moved down. Which firms not on the original list have surfaced through the work. The list is alive, not fixed.
rows.Task: Refresh Tier A at the 6-month mark

rows.Notes: Of the LinkedIn network of thousands, who has credible warm-intro reach into each Tier A firm. Not just any connection: credible. The intro-er has to carry standing the target reader respects.
rows.Task: Build warm-intro architecture from current network into Tier A

rows.Notes: For each Tier A firm: who's the right reader? Often the head of platform, sometimes the GP, sometimes both. The work reaches both. Map the named individuals, not just the firm.
rows.Task: Map named partners and platform leads at each Tier A firm

rows.Notes: Tier A finalized at 9 firms: Forerunner, Lerer Hippeau, Costanoa, M13, True Ventures, Maveron, Slow Ventures, Initialized Capital (watch), Greycroft (watch). 5 original candidates moved to Tier B: Spark Capital (too large), Homebrew (evergreen model, no LP capital), Cowboy Ventures (below AUM floor), Defy Partners (below AUM floor), Founder Collective (below AUM floor). BoxGroup also Tier B (4-person team). 3 slots remain open to fill as the work surfaces new candidates.

rows.Task: Qualify the candidate firm list against the ICP signals

rows.Notes: For Tier A firms where no warm path exists. Triggered by a specific event: a published Field Notes piece, a portfolio move, a new platform hire. Cold but contextual, never broadcast.
rows.Task: Build the cold-approach playbook

rows.Notes: Which firm. Which trigger. Which language. Probably tied to a Field Notes piece that's landed. The first deliberate cold approach is a moment to design, not improvise.
rows.Task: Make the first deliberate cold approach

rows.Notes: Tier A Pipeline database created on The Narrow Door page. 12 firms pre-loaded at Mapped stage with named GPs and first next actions. URL:
rows.Task: Stand up the active relationship pipeline at the target tier

rows.Notes: Per the brief: the single test. For every artifact produced, would a target-tier partner read this, recognize Sightbox as peer to their own thinking, want to continue. Walk the surfaces produced so far through the test as a discipline, not just an instinct.
rows.Task: Stress-test all artifacts against the partner-peer test

rows.Notes: Per the brief: as the build produces sharpened claims, published pieces, case studies, targeting intelligence, compile back into the canon. Substrate gets richer as the build progresses. Quarterly cadence, at minimum.
rows.Task: Compile new substance back into canon (quarterly)

rows.Notes: Per the brief: when a session produces a real decision or artifact, log it. As session log, build-area page update, or compiled canon entry. Set up the logging discipline so it's frictionless from the start.
rows.Task: Set up the session-log discipline

rows.Notes: End of first 90 days. Take stock: foundation laid? Category claim sharper, first Field Notes shipped, case study framework prototyped, Tier A named. If yes, the next 90 days shift toward distribution and small-surface contact. If no, name what still needs to be foundational.
rows.Task: 90-day review of the foundation

rows.Notes: Atlas pattern: capture during work, synthesize at the end, walk weekly for coherence. The build compounds across areas only if walked weekly. Sharpening in one area should leave the others with better material.
rows.Task: Walk all four build areas weekly for coherence

rows.Notes: End of second 90 days. The phase about distribution and small-surface contact with the target tier. Has it happened? Are Field Notes reaching named partners? Have any conversations started? Walk the signals.
rows.Task: 180-day review of distribution

rows.Notes: End of the third 90-day block. The phase about first deliberate engagements at the target tier. The credentialing engagement is the destination. By 12 months, is one in motion? If yes, the 4.0 build is doing its work.
rows.Task: 12-month review: is a credentialing engagement in motion

rows.Notes: Per the brief: spend time in one area per session, but stay aware of how it loads the other three. Decide what working in this project actually looks like week to week. Where does a session start? What does Atlas capture look like? Get the operational rhythm right early.
rows.Task: Establish the weekly Sightbox 4.0 working rhythm

rows.Notes: When a session is the artifact itself, write a session log. The May 25, 2026 origin diagnosis is the model. Conversations that produce real insight don't disappear; they get logged.
rows.Task: Write session logs when the conversation is the artifact
